environment.description: Same Ktor service on EKS 1.28 with nCipher nShield Connect XC. HSM configured with strict Security World policy: OCS-protected key set with k-of-n=2-of-3 cardset required for key generation, but operational use delegated to module-only protection. The JCE provider registration in java.security lists ONLY 'nCipherKM' as provider #1 with property 'nCipherKM.disableSoftwareFallback=true'. The PKCS12 keystore path is NOT mounted (Kubernetes Secret not bound to this namespace). Additionally, the HSM firmware policy (v13.4.4) enforces that the 'crypto.keyAlias' must match a pre-registered key handle in the Security World - arbitrary alias strings return PKCS#11 CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID. Pod seccomp profile (RuntimeDefault) and the node's SELinux context (container_crypto_t) restrict file reads to /opt/keys/* but the Secret simply doesn't exist in this namespace.

config.hsm: nCipher nShield Connect XC, firmware 13.4.4, Security World with OCS 2-of-3
config.software_keystore: NOT MOUNTED - Secret 'signing-keystore' not bound to namespace 'prod-signing'
config.network_policy: egress only to HSM endpoint 10.0.50.10:9004, deny-all other
config.hsm_firmware_policy: key alias must match pre-registered handle, CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID on mismatch
